questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 13-year-old boy presents with involuntary dancing movements of his right hand. He was diagnosed with rheumatic fever. What constitutes the ganglia involved in the presenting complication?
questions.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of Sydenham's chorea, a complication of rheumatic fever. The choreic movements are caused by destruction of D2 neurons of the striatum. The neostriatum consists of the caudate nucleus and putamen. The source further gives the nomenclature: corpus striatum = caudate nucleus + putamen + globus pallidus; lentiform nucleus = putamen + globus pallidus; neostriatum = caudate nucleus + putamen.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding the lentiform complex?

options.text: The internal capsule separates the lentiform complex from caudate nucleus
The external capsule separates the claustrum from putamen
Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the internal medullary lamina
Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the external medullary lamina

questions.correctAnswerText: Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the internal medullary lamina
questions.explanation: Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the external medullary lamina, so the statement that they are separated by the internal medullary lamina is false. From deep to superficial, the source lists: caudate nucleus; internal capsule; globus pallidus internal; internal medullary lamina; globus pallidus external; external medullary lamina; putamen; external capsule; claustrum; extreme capsule; insular cortex.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Wilson's pencils are related to?
questions.explanation: Wilson's pencils are thin myelinated or unmyelinated axons that are afferents and efferents passing through the striatum. The source shows a micrograph of putamen and external globus pallidus with Wilson's pencils as blue diagonal linear structures.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 64-year-old man presented with a reduced range of motion in his limbs. On examination, cogwheel rigidity and resting tremors were noticed. What is the direct pathway involved in this disorder?

options.text: Cortex > Striatum > Globus pallidus > Subthalamic nucleus > Premotor cortex
Cortex > Striatum > Globus pallidus > Thalamus > Premotor cortex
Cortex > Globus pallidus > Subthalamic nucleus > Thalamus > Premotor cortex
Cortex > Globus pallidus > Striatum > Thalamus > Premotor cortex

questions.correctAnswerText: Cortex > Striatum > Globus pallidus > Thalamus > Premotor cortex
questions.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of Parkinson disease, involving destruction of the substantia nigra in the basal ganglia. The source gives the direct pathway as cortex > striatum > globus pallidus > thalamus > premotor cortex. The indirect pathway is cortex > striatum > globus pallidus externa > subthalamic nucleus > globus pallidus interna and substantia nigra reticulata > thalamus > premotor cortex. The direct pathway stimulates movement and the indirect pathway inhibits movement.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A man presented with sudden violent flinging movements confined to the proximal parts of the right limb. This condition is caused due to the lesion involving which structure?
questions.explanation: A lesion in the subthalamic nucleus causes sudden, violent, involuntary movements on one side of the body, commonly affecting proximal extremity musculature, called hemiballismus. The movements are contralateral to the side of the lesion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of the limbic system?
questions.explanation: Medial thalamic nuclei are not part of the limbic system; the anterior nucleus of the thalamus is part of it. The limbic system controls emotional behavior and participates in conversion of short-term memory to long-term memory. It contains both grey and white matter and lies between the cerebral cortex and hypothalamus. The source diagram includes cingulate gyrus, hippocampus, amygdaloid body, hypothalamus, mammillary body, fornix and pineal region relationships.
